sections.content: -kor attaches to a number or time word to mean 'at [that time]'. It doesn't change for vowel harmony -- it's one of the few Hungarian suffixes that stays -kor regardless of the word it attaches to.

items.english: Do we want to meet at seven?

sections.content: hétkor is built from hét ('seven') plus -kor, with no linking vowel needed. Unlike most Hungarian suffixes, -kor never changes to -kör or -kar -- it's an exception to vowel harmony worth just memorising.
